## One draw is now a whole dataset

An estimator is a function of the sample, so it is a **random variable**. Its distribution is the **sampling distribution**, and every question we ask about an estimator is an expectation over it.

```{r eval=FALSE}
theta_hats <- replicate(k, {
  x <- rmodel(n, theta)   # simulate a whole dataset of size n
  estimator(x)            # collapse it to one number
})
```

- $n$ is the usually given by the a real data set
- $k$ is your our choice: time vs. precision of estimate

## Bias, variance, and MSE

$$\text{Bias}(\hat\theta) = \E{\hat\theta} - \theta, \qquad
\text{MSE}(\hat \theta) = \E{(\hat \theta - \theta)^2} = \Var{\hat\theta} + \text{Bias}(\hat\theta)^2$$

- All three are expectation, estimate using mean of $\hat\theta - \theta$, or $(\hat\theta - \theta)^2$.
- MSE balance accuracy and precision
- The ranking can depend on $n$, so **try several $n$** 

## Coverage and Expected Width

$$\text{coverage} = P(A \le \theta \le B) = \E{\ind(A \le \theta \le B)}$$

- Replicate samples with known $\theta$, create CI for each sample, proportion that include true $\theta$  
- Coverage is a proportion out of $k$: report `binom.test(hits, k)$conf.int` alongside it.
- After establishing coverage, compare different CI methods on **expected width** $\E{B - A}$.
